intent: "Who is in this campaign?" and "where is this person across everything?" — the same read from either end, and with historical participations included on request.

input_schema.title: enrollment.list input
input_schema.description: One page of the people the provider holds in one campaign. The campaign is named as campaign.get names it: by a first link, or by the pin.

external_id.description: The provider's own identifier, given to link a campaign for the first time. Later calls work by the pin.

limit.description: At most this many people on the page. Required: absence is not a default, and a page may come back shorter.

offset.description: Where the page starts in the provider's own order: 0 for the first page, then the previous page's `offset` plus the number of items it returned.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

total.description: The provider's own count of the people in the campaign, or null when it refused to count them. Never the length of this page.

external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the person. Reported, never pinned: a read pins nobody.

first_name.description: Null when the provider holds no first name, an empty one included.

last_name.description: Null when the provider holds no last name, an empty one included.

status.description: Where the person stands in the campaign. `other` is the honest answer for a state this vocabulary has no word for; the provider's own word is under `vendor.status_in_sequence` either way.

current_step.description: The provider's own label for the step the person is at, or null when it names none. A label, not a number: providers number steps differently, and some do not number them at all.

added_at.description: When the provider added the person to the campaign, in UTC; null when it does not say.

opted_out.description: Whether the provider holds the person as opted out.

vendor.description: The provider's own words for what the neutral fields above summarise. A closed list, so no address, name or message text can travel here.

has_more.description: Whether the provider holds more people after this page.

ordering.description: The provider's own order, the one `offset` counts in: the most recently added first.

campaign.description: The provider's identifier for the campaign this read listed, pinned the first time as campaign.get pins it.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no campaign under the identifier this call carried.
The provider account's plan or role does not include this capability, so no call by this account can answer it.
The provider's answer was larger than this installation lets a plugin read from a program (`Plugins:Exec:OutputBytes`), so it was cut off; asking again would cut it the same way.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read the people in a campaign for this account.
The provider refused the read for now and it may be asked again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing and costs nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

conformance: A page holds at most `limit` people, starting at `offset` in the provider's own order, and `has_more` says whether more follow.

A page may come back short of `limit` with `has_more: true`: the plugin stops before the result would pass 768 KiB, counted as the runtime counts it (six bytes for DEL, for every character outside ASCII and for each of `<`, `>`, `&`, `'`, `"`, `+` and the backtick, twelve for one outside the Basic Multilingual Plane).
The next page starts at `offset` plus the number of items this page returned, never at `offset + limit`.
A call carrying only `campaign.external_ids.campaign` answers, and a call carrying only `args.campaign.external_id` answers and returns that identifier under `external_ids.campaign`.
A campaign the provider does not hold fails `campaign_not_found` as permanent, rather than answering an empty page.
No person's address appears anywhere in the result, `vendor` included.
`total` is the provider's own count, or null when the provider refused to count; it is never the length of the page.
A state this vocabulary has no word for is `other`, with the provider's own word under `vendor.status_in_sequence`.
A name the provider holds as empty is null, never an empty string.
A read creates nothing and pins no person: the only identifier it returns under `external_ids` is the campaign's.
